forbidden: provenance (id-bearing; permitted only for the quorum distinctness predicate)
grade (configuration attribute: granted on actor, required on a source gate; never a token field)
note: A guard states a governance condition over declared token properties; it never computes. `reversibility` and `uncertainty` are ordered declared properties admitted on the same terms as `risk`: the token asserts them, the language compares them, and nothing derives them. Admitting a host-computed value as a declared property is how an autonomy function stays outside the notation — the wall below is about what the NOTATION may do, not about what a host may hand it. `tags` is a set of declared, non-id categories; membership (`contains`) is not computation, mirroring the quorum distinctness already evaluated over provenance. Which tags exist and what they trigger is policy. `grade` is a configuration attribute (granted on actor, required on a source gate), not a token property, and is therefore never guardable — listed explicitly in `forbidden`. This is the wall between an expressive notation and a programming language.
